display_title: Official Review of Paper1583 by Reviewer gX4Y

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a modification to denoising diffusion GAN, where in the first denoising step, the latent variable changes to a semantic representation learned by an encoder. The encoder is trained with reconstruction objective with the generator as the decoder. The purpose f doing so is that the first denoising step of DDGAN determines the semantics, and later steps work on refining the details. Results show that the model obtains better performance than DDGAN baseline, and it also provides an semantically meaningful representation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

1. This is an interesting idea of training diffusion based models: enforce the semantics to be determined in the first step, and therefore remaining steps can be used to refine the details. The way to implementing it as a semantic encoder is also interesting.

2. The method is clearly illustrated with pictures and descriptions, making readers easy to follow

3. The ablation study clearly presents the effect of each component in the model and provide insights to analyze the model. Results also show some improvements with fewer sampling steps on CelebAHQ.


Weakness:

1. The paper claim that the latent vector from the encoder is shown to be semantically meaningful, which can be exploited on various downstream tasks. However, I do not see any experimental evidence to support this argument.

2. In Table 1, it seems like constraint on training the encoder as well as the progressive pipeline will hurt the performance, but then why they are introduced? If the purpose is to maintain a semantic meaningful latent, then again there is no downstream task for showing that. The semantics part in section 5.2 is insufficient, because we do not want to sacrifice sample quality just for better interpolation results.

3.  The improvements over DDGAN is not significant, especially on CIFAR-10, and it is hard to justify the merits with the results.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well written and clear. The novelty is a bit limited, as it is a small modification to DDGAN. Reproducibility should not be hard because its implementation is largely based on DDGAN.
content.summary_of_the_review: While this paper proposes an interesting idea to improve DDGAN, the empirical results are not strong enough to support the modification. I tentatively incline to rejection, but will be happy to raise the score if my concerns are addressed.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes two approaches to increase the performance of diffusion models at test time with only few sampling steps while also containing a semantically meaningful latent space. To achieve this the paper builds on top of Denoising Diffusion GANs and Diffusion Autoencoders. The core contributions are to predict $x_0$ at each time step (instead of the noise epsilon) which is enabled by a new timestep schedule. Evaluation on CelebA-HQ and CIFAR10 show improved quantitative results with only 2 model evaluations at test time.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper proposes to combine Diffusion Autoencoders with Denoising Diffusion GANs to achieve a model that can produce samples with very sampling steps while also providing a semantically meaningful latent space.
The denoising process is reformulated such that the model predicts the clean $x_0$ at each time step and a new timestep schedule is proposed such that the model focuses on semantic layout for a larget T and on perceptual quality and details for t < T.

While the paper shows good results on some datasets I have some concerns:
- predicting $x_0$ instead of the noise (or $x_{t-1}$ or some other parametrization) is not a novel interpretation; even the original DDPM paper tried that but stated that it affected the resulting image quality negatively (see page 4 of the DDPM paper: *There is also the possibility of predicting x0, but we found this to lead to worse sample quality early in our experiments.*); there are also other approaches that predict a linear interpolation between the noise and $x_0$ [1] or both at the same time [2]
- there is not much novelty in the model architecture itself, it is mostly just a combination of Diffusion Autoencoders and Denoising Diffusion GANs
- experiments are only performed on relatively simple datasets (CIFAR10 and CelebA); it is not clear that this approach would scale to more complex datasets (e.g. ImageNet or LAION400M)
- there is no evidence that the semantically meaningful latent code is actually useful (there is only interpolation done); ideally, it would be shown that it is actually useful, e.g., for editing images or controlling the image generation process; there is also the Perceptual Path Length introduced in the StyleGAN paper to evaluate if the latent codes are (somewhat) continuous which could be a proxy for being meaningful
- Table 1 should also include recall since right now it seems that the simple combination of Diffusion Autoencoder and Denoising Diffusion GANs performs best

Minor: in Fig 3, the bottom right start and end face seem to be almost identical?

[1] Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models, ICLR, 2022
[2] Dynamic Dual-Output Diffusion Models, CVPR, 2022
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is clearly written and easy to understand. Most of the experiments should be reproducible from the descriptions.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall the paper proposes some interesting combinations and techniques but I feel that the overall novelty is still somewhat limited and there are some facts to be addressed.
The paper states several times that it interprets the sampling process completely new by predicting $x_0$, something that has been done previously. The split into semantic and refinement stage is interesting but I'm not convinced it fits into the diffusion model framework. The authors explicitly state that using the large T to destroy all content does not follow the Gaussian assumption anymore.
Also, the evaluation is only done on relatively simple datasets and there is little evaluation of how useful the semantic latent space is besides interpolation between images.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors target to simultaneously resolve the two issues in denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs): time-expensive sampling process and the semantically meaningless latent space. They propose to replace the denoising process with a refinement process by generating semantics first and then refining details progressively. As a result, they show competitive generation performance in only two sampling steps with meaningful latent space.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
*************************
Strengths
*************************
+ Clear exposition: well-organized demos and clear writing.
+ Reasonable motivation.
+ Easy to reproduce.

*************************
Weaknesses
*************************

- Technical novelty is incremental.
  - It is a trivial combination between Denoising Diffusion GAN in the semantic generation stage and Diffusion Autoencoder in the refinement stage.

- Technical details are questionable.
  - Since resolving the time-expensive sampling is one of the major motivations, please articulate the justification why not build your work on top of LDM, which is at least 10x faster than non-latent diffusion and achieves the best FID according to Table 2. 

- Experiments are unconvincing.
  - CIFAR-10 is too toy-like for conditional generation. The authors are highly suggested to experiment on the golden standard ImageNet and FFHQ (for unconditional generation) so as to directly compare to the recent SOTA StyleGAN-XL [r1].
  - Fatally, the authors are not aware of the recent SOTA StyleGAN-XL [r1]. Considering the proposed method is worse than LDM in Table 2 and worse than StyleGAN2+ADA and many other methods in Table 3, very likely it would be inferior to StyleGAN-XL on the larger-scale golden standard FFHQ and ImageNet datasets. Please refer to their significant improvements over StyleGAN2 (ADA is no longer critical for larger-scale datasets) and over CDM/ADM (representative DDPMs). In the case if the proposed method is inferior to StyleGAN-XL, their motivation to resolve the two issues in DDPMs turns shaky, because StyleGAN-XL does not have such two issues by nature. Therefore, it is critical to compare to StyleGAN-XL on larger-scale dataset in the next round of submission.

[r1] Sauer, Axel, Katja Schwarz, and Andreas Geiger. "Stylegan-xl: Scaling stylegan to large diverse datasets." SIGGRAPH 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clear exposition: well-organized demos and clear writing.

Incremental technical novelty.

Easy to reproduce.
